lessons.title: My Family: Getting to Know Mai's Family
lessons.description: In this lesson, learners will read about a family and practice finding the main idea and specific details in a short text.

sections.heading: Finding the Main Idea
sections.content: The main idea is what the text is mostly about. It tells you the most important information. Often, you can find the main idea in the first or last sentence.

sections.heading: Example: Main Idea
sections.content: If a text starts with 'Hi! My name is Mai. I live with my family.', the main idea is probably about Mai's family. Look for repeated words or ideas.

sections.heading: Look for Keywords
sections.content: When you read, look for keywords that are repeated. These words can help you understand the main topic. For example, if you see 'mother,' 'father,' and 'brother' many times, the text is about family.

passage.title: Mai's Family
passage.content: Hi! My name is Mai. I am 7 years old. I live with my family in Hanoi. My family is small. I have a mother and a father. My mother's name is Lan. She is a teacher. My father's name is Nam. He is an engineer. I also have a little brother. His name is An. He is 3 years old. We like to play together. I love my family very much.

questions.stemText: What is the main topic of this passage?
How old is Mai?
What is Mai's mother's job?
What is Mai's father's name?
How many brothers does Mai have?
Where does Mai live?
What do Mai and her brother like to do together?
How does Mai feel about her family?

lessons.title: Pets and Animals: Learning About Linh's Dog
lessons.description: This lesson helps learners identify specific information in a text about pets and understand simple descriptions of animals.

sections.heading: Scanning for Details
sections.content: Scanning means quickly looking for specific words or numbers in a text. You don't need to read every word. Just move your eyes fast to find what you are looking for.

sections.heading: Example: Scanning
sections.content: If a question asks 'What color is the dog?', you can scan the text for the word 'dog' and then look for a color word near it, like 'brown' or 'black'.

sections.heading: Use Keywords to Scan
sections.content: When a question asks 'What is the dog's name?', look for the word 'name' or 'is called' near 'dog'. This helps you find the answer quickly without reading slowly.

passage.title: Linh and Lucky
passage.content: I have a pet dog. His name is Lucky. Lucky is small and brown. He likes to play with a red ball. Every morning, I walk Lucky in the park. We see many animals there. I see a big cat sleeping under a tree. Birds sing in the sky. Sometimes, I see a small rabbit eating green grass. I like animals very much. They are cute and fun to watch.

questions.stemText: What kind of pet does Linh have?
What is the dog's name?
What color is Lucky?
What does Lucky like to play with?
Where does Linh walk Lucky every morning?
What animal does Linh see sleeping under a tree?
What do birds do in the sky?
How does Linh feel about animals?

lessons.title: Food I Like: Exploring An's Favorite Foods
lessons.description: This lesson focuses on identifying preferences and understanding simple descriptions of food items in a reading passage.

sections.heading: Understanding Preferences
sections.content: When someone talks about 'food I like' or 'my favorite food,' they are telling you what they prefer. Look for words like 'like,' 'love,' 'favorite,' or 'enjoy' to find out what they prefer.

sections.heading: Example: Preferences
sections.content: If the text says 'I like pizza very much,' it means pizza is a food the person enjoys. If it says 'My favorite fruit is mango,' then mango is their top choice.

sections.heading: Match Words to Pictures (Implicit)
sections.content: Even without pictures, try to imagine the food. If you read 'rice' and 'pho,' think about what they look like and how they taste. This helps you remember the information better.

passage.title: An's Favorite Foods
passage.content: My name is An. I love food! My favorite food is pho. It is a delicious noodle soup. I eat pho for breakfast sometimes. I also like rice with chicken. My mother cooks it for dinner. For fruit, I like mangoes. They are sweet and yellow. I drink water every day, but sometimes I drink orange juice. I do not like coffee. It is bitter. Eating good food makes me happy!

questions.stemText: What is An's favorite food?
What does An sometimes eat for breakfast?
Who cooks rice with chicken for An?
What color are mangoes that An likes?
What does An drink every day?
What food does An NOT like?
How does eating good food make An feel?
What kind of food is pho?

lessons.title: My School Day: A Look at Lan's Morning
lessons.description: Learners will read about a typical school day and practice sequencing events and identifying key activities.

sections.heading: Understanding Sequence of Events
sections.content: When a text talks about a day, it often tells you things in order. Look for words like 'first,' 'then,' 'after that,' 'in the morning,' 'in the afternoon' to understand the order of events.

sections.heading: Example: Sequence
sections.content: If the text says 'First, I eat breakfast. Then, I go to school,' you know eating breakfast happens before going to school. This helps you put events in the correct order.

sections.heading: Visualize the Day
sections.content: As you read about someone's day, try to imagine what they are doing. This helps you remember the order of activities and understand the passage better.

passage.title: Lan's School Morning
passage.content: My name is Lan. I am a student. Every weekday, I wake up at 6 o'clock. First, I brush my teeth and wash my face. Then, I eat a quick breakfast with my family. My mother makes delicious banh mi. After breakfast, I put on my school uniform. My school bag is ready. At 7 o'clock, I ride my bicycle to school. School starts at 7:30. My favorite subject is English. I like learning new words. School is fun!

questions.stemText: What time does Lan wake up?
What does Lan do first after waking up?
What does Lan's mother make for breakfast?
How does Lan go to school?
What time does school start?
What is Lan's favorite subject?
What does Lan like about English?
What kind of days does Lan go to school?

lessons.title: Colors and Shapes: Describing Objects in a Room
lessons.description: This lesson helps learners identify colors and shapes of common objects, practicing descriptive vocabulary.

sections.heading: Identifying Descriptions
sections.content: When you read, look for words that describe things. These are often adjectives like 'big,' 'small,' 'red,' 'blue,' 'round,' or 'square.' They tell you more about a noun.

sections.heading: Example: Descriptions
sections.content: If the text says 'a red ball,' 'red' describes the color of the ball. If it says 'a square table,' 'square' describes the shape of the table. Pay attention to these words.

sections.heading: Picture the Object
sections.content: Try to create a mental picture of the object as you read its description. If it says 'a yellow circle,' imagine a yellow circle. This helps with comprehension.

passage.title: My Colorful Room
passage.content: My room is small but nice. I have a bed. My blanket is blue. On the wall, there is a big, red clock. It is round. Next to my bed, there is a small, brown table. It is square. I have many toys. My favorite toy car is green. I also have a yellow box for my books. On the floor, there is a soft, white rug. I like all the colors in my room!

questions.stemText: What color is the blanket on the bed?
What shape is the clock on the wall?
What color is the clock?
What shape is the table next to the bed?
What color is the favorite toy car?
What is the yellow box for?
What color is the rug on the floor?
How does the writer feel about the colors in their room?

lessons.title: My Home: Exploring a Vietnamese House
lessons.description: Learners will read about different rooms in a house and practice identifying locations and functions of rooms.

sections.heading: Understanding Location
sections.content: When you read about a house, pay attention to words that tell you 'where' things are. Words like 'in,' 'on,' 'next to,' 'upstairs,' 'downstairs' help you understand the layout.

sections.heading: Example: Location
sections.content: If the text says 'The kitchen is next to the living room,' you know their positions relative to each other. 'My bedroom is upstairs' tells you its floor.

sections.heading: Draw a Simple Map (Mentally)
sections.content: As you read about the rooms in a house, try to imagine a simple floor plan in your mind. This helps you visualize where everything is and makes it easier to answer questions about location.

passage.title: My House in Vietnam
passage.content: I live in a house with my family. Our house has two floors. Downstairs, there is a living room. We watch TV and talk there. Next to the living room is the kitchen. My mother cooks delicious food in the kitchen. We eat in the dining room, which is also downstairs. Upstairs, there are two bedrooms. My parents' bedroom is big. My bedroom is smaller, but I like it. There is also a bathroom upstairs. Our house is always clean and cozy.

questions.stemText: How many floors does the house have?
What do they do in the living room?
Where is the kitchen located?
Who cooks in the kitchen?
Where do they eat their meals?
How many bedrooms are upstairs?
Which bedroom is bigger?
How is their house described?

lessons.title: The Weather: Talking About Today's Weather
lessons.description: Learners will read about different weather conditions and practice identifying current weather and related activities.

sections.heading: Understanding Weather Vocabulary
sections.content: Weather words like 'sunny,' 'rainy,' 'cold,' 'hot,' 'windy' help us understand what the sky and air are like. Pay attention to these words to know the weather.

sections.heading: Example: Weather Words
sections.content: If the text says 'It is rainy today,' you know it's raining. If it says 'The sun is shining,' it means it's sunny. These words tell you the weather directly.

sections.heading: Connect Weather to Activities
sections.content: People often do different things depending on the weather. If it's hot, they might swim. If it's cold, they wear a jacket. Connecting weather to activities helps you understand the text better.

passage.title: Today's Weather
passage.content: Today is a beautiful day! The sun is shining brightly, and the sky is blue. It is warm, but not too hot. I like sunny weather. Yesterday, it was rainy. I stayed home and read a book. Tomorrow, the weather forecast says it will be a little windy. I will fly my kite in the park. My mother says winter is coming soon. It will be cold then. I need my warm jacket for winter. I hope it doesn't rain too much!

questions.stemText: What is the weather like today?
What color is the sky today?
What was the weather like yesterday?
What did the writer do yesterday?
What will the weather be like tomorrow?
What will the writer do tomorrow?
What season is coming soon?
What does the writer need for winter?

lessons.title: Daily Routines: My Morning Routine
lessons.description: This lesson helps learners understand a sequence of daily activities and practice identifying specific actions and times.

sections.heading: Understanding Time Markers
sections.content: Time markers like 'at 7 o'clock,' 'in the morning,' 'after,' 'before' help you understand when actions happen. Pay close attention to these words to follow the routine.

sections.heading: Example: Time Markers
sections.content: If the text says 'I wake up at 6 AM. Then I eat breakfast,' you know waking up is at 6 AM and breakfast is after that. This helps you order the events.

sections.heading: Create a Mental Checklist
sections.content: As you read about a daily routine, try to make a mental checklist of the actions. What happens first? What happens next? This helps you remember the order of events.

passage.title: My Morning Routine
passage.content: Every morning, I wake up at 6:30 AM. First, I go to the bathroom to wash my face and brush my teeth. Then, I get dressed in my school uniform. At 7:00 AM, I go to the kitchen. My mother makes a simple breakfast for me, usually bread and milk. I eat quickly. After breakfast, I pack my school bag and check my homework. At 7:45 AM, I say goodbye to my family and walk to school. My school starts at 8:00 AM. I am always on time!

questions.stemText: What time does the writer wake up?
What does the writer do after washing their face and brushing their teeth?
What does the mother usually make for breakfast?
What time does the writer go to the kitchen?
What does the writer do after breakfast?
options: Pack school bag and check homework

questions.stemText: How does the writer go to school?
What time does school start?
How does the writer describe their punctuality for school?

lessons.title: Numbers and Time: Learning About a Schedule
lessons.description: This lesson helps learners practice identifying numbers and times in a schedule and understanding simple numerical information.

sections.heading: Finding Numbers and Times
sections.content: Numbers tell us 'how many' or 'what time.' When you read, look for digits (1, 2, 3) or words for numbers (one, two, three). Time is often shown with numbers and 'o'clock' or 'AM/PM'.

sections.heading: Example: Numbers and Time
sections.content: If the text says 'I have 3 books' or 'School starts at 8:00 AM,' the numbers '3' and '8:00' are important details. Scan for these specific pieces of information.

sections.heading: Match Numbers to Questions
sections.content: If a question asks 'How many?' or 'What time?', scan the text specifically for numbers. Don't get distracted by other words. This helps you find the answer quickly.

passage.title: My Saturday Schedule
passage.content: Saturdays are busy for me! I wake up at 7:00 AM. At 8:00 AM, I eat breakfast with my family. We have 4 people in my family. From 9:00 AM to 10:00 AM, I help my mother clean the house. At 10:30 AM, I go to the park with my friends. We play for 2 hours. So, we finish playing at 12:30 PM. In the afternoon, I read 1 book. At 6:00 PM, we eat dinner. I go to bed at 9:00 PM. It's a long day!

questions.stemText: What time does the writer wake up on Saturday?
How many people are in the writer's family?
What time does the writer help clean the house?
What time does the writer go to the park?
How long do they play at the park?
What time do they finish playing at the park?
How many books does the writer read in the afternoon?
What time does the writer go to bed?

lessons.title: My Friends: Learning About Friendship
lessons.description: This lesson helps learners understand descriptions of friends and identify shared activities and feelings about friendship.

sections.heading: Understanding Relationships
sections.content: When you read about friends, look for words that describe what they do together or how they feel about each other. Words like 'play with,' 'talk to,' 'happy,' 'best friend' are clues.

sections.heading: Example: Relationships
sections.content: If the text says 'My friend Linh is kind,' you learn about Linh's personality. If it says 'We play football every Sunday,' you know a shared activity. These details build understanding.

sections.heading: Identify Shared Activities
sections.content: When reading about friends, pay attention to the verbs that describe what they do together. This helps you understand their bond and common interests.

passage.title: My Best Friend, Hoa
passage.content: I have many friends at school, but my best friend is Hoa. She is 8 years old, like me. Hoa has long, black hair and a big smile. She is very kind and funny. We always sit together in class. After school, we often play in the park. We like to swing and slide. Sometimes, we draw pictures or read books at my house. Hoa helps me with my homework when I don't understand. I help her too. We laugh a lot together. I am very happy to have Hoa as my friend.

questions.stemText: Who is the writer's best friend?
How old is Hoa?
What does Hoa look like?
options: Long, black hair and a big smile
Brown hair and a quiet face

questions.stemText: What do the friends do after school?
What do they like to do in the park?
What do they sometimes do at the writer's house?
What does Hoa help the writer with?
How does the writer feel about having Hoa as a friend?

lessons.title: Going Shopping: A Trip to the Market
lessons.description: Learners will read about a shopping trip and practice identifying items bought and understanding simple transactions.

sections.heading: Identifying Items and Actions
sections.content: When reading about shopping, look for the names of things people buy. Also, pay attention to verbs like 'buy,' 'sell,' 'pay' to understand the actions related to shopping.

sections.heading: Example: Shopping Details
sections.content: If the text says 'I bought three apples,' you know the item and the quantity. If it says 'The market is busy,' you understand the atmosphere. These details are important.

sections.heading: Focus on 'What' and 'Where'
sections.content: When reading about shopping, ask yourself 'What did they buy?' and 'Where did they go?' These questions will help you find the most important information in the passage.

passage.title: My Trip to the Market
passage.content: Today, I went to the market with my mother. The market was very busy and noisy. First, we bought some fresh vegetables: green spinach and red tomatoes. Then, we went to the fruit stall. My mother bought two big mangoes and a bunch of small, sweet grapes. I like grapes! After that, we bought some fresh fish for dinner. The fish seller was friendly. We didn't buy any meat today. My mother paid with money. Shopping at the market is fun, but sometimes it is tiring.

questions.stemText: Who did the writer go to the market with?
How was the market described?
What vegetables did they buy?
How many mangoes did they buy?
What other fruit did they buy?
What did they buy for dinner?
Did they buy any meat today?
How did the mother pay?

lessons.title: In the Park: A Sunny Afternoon
lessons.description: This lesson helps learners identify activities and objects found in a park, practicing vocabulary related to outdoor spaces.

sections.heading: Identifying Setting and Activities
sections.content: The 'setting' is where the story happens, like a park. 'Activities' are what people do there. Look for words that describe the place and the actions happening in it.

sections.heading: Example: Setting and Activities
sections.content: If the text says 'We went to the park. My friends played football,' you know the place is a park and the activity is playing football. These are key details.

sections.heading: Imagine the Scene
sections.content: As you read about the park, try to imagine yourself there. What do you see? What do you hear? What are people doing? This helps you understand the text better.

passage.title: Fun in the Park
passage.content: It was a sunny afternoon, so my family went to the park. The park is big and has many green trees. My little brother, An, ran to the playground. He loves the slide and the swings. My father sat on a bench and read a newspaper. My mother walked around and looked at the flowers. I rode my bicycle on the path. Many children were playing football on the grass. Some people were having a picnic under a big tree. It was a happy day for everyone.

questions.stemText: What was the weather like when they went to the park?
Who went to the park with the writer?
What does the little brother, An, love at the playground?
options: The climbing frame and monkey bars

questions.stemText: What did the father do in the park?
What did the mother do?
options: Walked around and looked at flowers

questions.stemText: What did the writer do in the park?
What were many children doing on the grass?
What were some people doing under a big tree?

lessons.title: My Bedroom: Describing My Personal Space
lessons.description: Learners will read about a bedroom and practice identifying objects and their locations within a room.

sections.heading: Understanding Spatial Relationships
sections.content: Spatial words like 'on,' 'under,' 'next to,' 'in front of,' 'behind' tell you where things are in relation to each other. These are important for understanding descriptions of a room.

sections.heading: Example: Spatial Words
sections.content: If the text says 'My bed is next to the window,' you know the bed's position. If it says 'Books are on the shelf,' you know where the books are. Look for these prepositions.

sections.heading: Visualize the Room
sections.content: Try to imagine the bedroom as you read. What furniture is there? Where are the items placed? A mental picture helps you remember details and answer questions about location.

passage.title: My Cozy Bedroom
passage.content: My bedroom is my favorite place in the house. It is small but very cozy. I have a comfortable bed with a soft, blue blanket. Next to my bed, there is a small table with a lamp. I read books there at night. In front of the window, there is a desk and a chair. I do my homework at this desk. On the wall, I have a picture of my family and a calendar. My clothes are in a big, brown wardrobe. My toys are in a box under the desk. I love my room!

questions.stemText: How is the writer's bedroom described?
What color is the blanket on the bed?
What is next to the bed?
options: A small table with a lamp

questions.stemText: What does the writer do at the small table?
Where is the desk and chair located?
What does the writer do at the desk?
What is on the wall?
options: A picture of family and a calendar

questions.stemText: Where are the writer's toys?
options: In a box under the desk

lessons.title: Fun at School: Recess and Learning
lessons.description: Learners will read about enjoyable activities at school and practice identifying specific events and feelings related to school life.

sections.heading: Identifying Positive Experiences
sections.content: When a text talks about 'fun' or 'happy' times, look for words that show enjoyment. These can be verbs like 'play,' 'laugh,' 'enjoy,' or adjectives like 'fun,' 'exciting,' 'happy'.

sections.heading: Example: Positive Experiences
sections.content: If the text says 'Recess is my favorite time because we play games,' you know playing games is a fun activity. This helps you understand what makes school enjoyable for the writer.

sections.heading: Look for Emotion Words
sections.content: Words like 'love,' 'like,' 'happy,' 'fun' tell you how the writer feels. These are important for understanding the overall tone and the writer's attitude towards school.

passage.title: My Fun School Day
passage.content: School is not just for learning; it's also for fun! My favorite part of the school day is recess. We go outside and play games. I love playing hide-and-seek with my friends, Linh and Minh. We laugh a lot! In class, I like art lessons. We draw and paint colorful pictures. My teacher, Ms. Hoa, is very kind. She always helps us. Sometimes, we sing songs in music class. Learning new things is exciting, especially when we do experiments in science. School is a great place to learn and play!

questions.stemText: What is the writer's favorite part of the school day?
What game does the writer love to play with friends?
Who are the writer's friends mentioned?
What do they do in art lessons?
Who is the writer's teacher?
What do they sometimes do in music class?
What makes learning new things exciting?
How does the writer feel about school?
options: It is a great place to learn and play.

lessons.title: Healthy Food: Eating Well with My Family
lessons.description: This lesson helps learners identify healthy food choices and understand the benefits of eating well.

sections.heading: Identifying Healthy Choices
sections.content: When reading about food, look for words that suggest something is good for you. Words like 'healthy,' 'fresh,' 'vitamins,' or 'strong' often point to healthy food choices.

sections.heading: Example: Healthy Food
sections.content: If the text says 'We eat many vegetables because they are healthy,' you know vegetables are good. If it says 'I drink water, not soda,' it shows a healthy drink choice.

sections.heading: Connect Food to Benefits
sections.content: Pay attention to why certain foods are mentioned. Is it for energy? To be strong? To stay healthy? Understanding the benefits helps you grasp the main message about healthy eating.

passage.title: Our Healthy Meals
passage.content: My family loves to eat healthy food. Every day, we eat a lot of fresh vegetables like spinach and carrots. My mother says vegetables make us strong. We also eat rice with fish or chicken. Fish is very good for our brains. For snacks, we eat fruit, not candy. My favorite fruits are bananas and oranges. They have many vitamins. We drink a lot of water throughout the day. We try not to eat too much sweet food or fast food. Eating healthy helps us stay active and happy!

questions.stemText: What kind of food does the writer's family love to eat?
What vegetables are mentioned in the passage?
Why does the mother say they should eat vegetables?
What do they eat with rice?
Why is fish good?
options: It is good for our brains.

questions.stemText: What do they eat for snacks instead of candy?
What are the writer's favorite fruits?
What helps them stay active and happy?

lessons.title: Seasons of the Year: Vietnam's Weather
lessons.description: This lesson helps learners identify different seasons and their typical weather conditions and activities in Vietnam.

sections.heading: Understanding Seasonal Changes
sections.content: Seasons bring different weather and activities. Look for words that describe the temperature (hot, cold), precipitation (rain, sun), and common things people do in each season.

sections.heading: Example: Seasonal Descriptions
sections.content: If the text says 'Summer is hot, and we go swimming,' you know the weather and an activity for summer. If it says 'Winter is cold, and I wear a jacket,' you learn about winter.

sections.heading: Connect Weather to Seasons
sections.content: Each season has typical weather. When you read about 'rainy' or 'sunny,' think about which season it usually happens in. This helps you link information.

passage.title: Seasons in My Country
passage.content: In Vietnam, we mostly have two main seasons: the dry season and the rainy season. But in the north, we also feel a bit of spring, summer, autumn, and winter. Spring is warm and fresh, with many flowers. Summer is very hot and sunny. We often go to the beach or swim in the pool. Autumn is cool and pleasant, my favorite season. Winter is a bit cold, especially in Hanoi. Sometimes, I need a warm coat. The rainy season brings a lot of rain, usually from May to October. I like all seasons, but autumn is the best!

questions.stemText: How many main seasons are there mostly in Vietnam?
What is the weather like in spring?
What do people often do in summer?
options: Go to the beach or swim

questions.stemText: What is the writer's favorite season?
What is the weather like in winter, especially in Hanoi?
What does the writer sometimes need in winter?
When is the rainy season usually?
How does the writer feel about autumn?

lessons.title: A Birthday Party: Celebrating with Friends
lessons.description: This lesson helps learners identify details about a birthday party, including activities, food, and gifts.

sections.heading: Identifying Party Details
sections.content: When reading about a party, look for who is there, what they eat, what games they play, and what gifts are given. These details help you understand the event.

sections.heading: Example: Party Details
sections.content: If the text says 'We ate cake and sang Happy Birthday,' you know the food and a common party activity. If it says 'My friend gave me a toy car,' you know about a gift.

sections.heading: Focus on the 5 Ws
sections.content: Ask yourself: Who is celebrating? What did they do? Where was it? When was it? Why are they celebrating? This helps you gather all the important information.

passage.title: Mai's Birthday Party
passage.content: Last Saturday was my friend Mai's birthday. She turned 8 years old! Her parents organized a party at her house. Many of our friends came. First, we played fun games like musical chairs and charades. Then, Mai opened her presents. She got a new doll, a colorful drawing book, and a big box of Lego. After that, we all sang 'Happy Birthday' and ate a delicious chocolate cake. There were also many snacks and fruit juice. We talked and laughed a lot. It was a wonderful party, and Mai was very happy!

questions.stemText: Whose birthday was it last Saturday?
How old did Mai turn?
Where was the party held?
What games did they play?
What was one of the gifts Mai received?
What kind of cake did they eat?
What did they drink at the party?
How did Mai feel about her party?

lessons.title: My Favorite Sport: Playing Badminton
lessons.description: This lesson helps learners identify details about a favorite sport, including equipment, location, and feelings about the activity.

sections.heading: Understanding Sports Vocabulary
sections.content: When reading about sports, look for specific words related to the game, like 'ball,' 'racket,' 'net,' 'team,' 'play,' 'win,' 'lose.' These words help you understand the sport.

sections.heading: Example: Sports Vocabulary
sections.content: If the text says 'I play football with a ball,' you know the equipment. If it says 'We play on a court,' you know the location. These details are important for comprehension.

sections.heading: Visualize the Game
sections.content: Try to imagine the sport as you read about it. What are the players doing? What does the equipment look like? This helps you connect the words to a real-world activity.

passage.title: My Love for Badminton
passage.content: My favorite sport is badminton. I play it every Sunday morning with my father. We go to the community center near our house. We need a racket and a shuttlecock to play. It's a fast game! My father is very good, but sometimes I win. We always have fun and get good exercise. I also like watching badminton on TV. My dream is to be a professional badminton player one day. It makes me feel strong and happy. I think it's a great sport for everyone in Vietnam!

questions.stemText: What is the writer's favorite sport?
When does the writer play badminton?
Who does the writer play badminton with?
Where do they play badminton?
What equipment do they need to play badminton?
How does the writer feel about playing badminton?
What is the writer's dream?
options: To be a professional badminton player

questions.stemText: How does playing badminton make the writer feel?

lessons.title: At the Zoo: Seeing Wild Animals
lessons.description: This lesson helps learners identify different animals and their characteristics, practicing vocabulary related to wildlife.

sections.heading: Identifying Animal Descriptions
sections.content: When reading about animals, look for words that describe what they look like (big, small, color), what they do (eat, sleep, run), and where they live. These details help you identify them.

sections.heading: Example: Animal Descriptions
sections.content: If the text says 'The elephant is big and grey,' you know its size and color. If it says 'Monkeys like to swing,' you know their activity. These are key descriptive elements.

sections.heading: Match Animals to Traits
sections.content: As you read, try to connect each animal with its unique characteristics or actions. For example, 'lions' with 'roar' or 'tall giraffes.' This helps you remember the information.

passage.title: My Day at the Zoo
passage.content: Last Sunday, my family and I went to the zoo. It was a sunny day. First, we saw the big, grey elephants. They were eating grass. Next, we saw some tall giraffes. They have long necks and brown spots. My favorite animals were the monkeys. They were very funny, swinging from tree to tree. We also saw a big lion sleeping. It looked very strong. There were many colorful birds too. We bought ice cream and juice. I love visiting the zoo because I can see many different animals!

What was the weather like at the zoo?

lessons.title: Weekend Plans: Fun Activities
lessons.description: This lesson helps learners identify planned activities for the weekend and understand simple future tense expressions.

sections.heading: Identifying Future Plans
sections.content: When reading about future plans, look for words like 'will,' 'going to,' 'tomorrow,' 'next week,' or specific days like 'Saturday,' 'Sunday.' These tell you what someone plans to do.

sections.heading: Example: Future Plans
sections.content: If the text says 'Tomorrow, I will visit my grandmother,' you know the action and when it will happen. If it says 'We are going to the beach on Sunday,' it's a future plan.

sections.heading: Look for Time Words
sections.content: Time words are crucial for understanding when events will take place. Scan for 'Saturday,' 'Sunday,' 'morning,' 'afternoon' to map out the weekend schedule.

passage.title: My Weekend Plans
passage.content: I love weekends because I don't have school! This Saturday morning, I will help my mother clean the house. In the afternoon, I am going to play football with my friends at the park. I hope it is sunny! On Sunday morning, my family and I will visit my grandparents. They live in the countryside. My grandmother always cooks delicious food. In the afternoon, I will read my new comic book. I also want to finish my homework so I can relax. It will be a busy but fun weekend!

questions.stemText: Why does the writer love weekends?
options: They can watch TV all day.
